title: Beat & Rhythm Skill
purpose: Understand tempo, beats, note durations, and how the melody sits on the rhythmic grid.

tempo.definition: Speed of the beat in beats per minute (BPM). One beat = 60/BPM seconds.

common.110-140: Upbeat — lively, more notes per phrase

note_durations_at_bpm.formula: whole=4 beats, half=2, quarter=1, eighth=0.5, sixteenth=0.25 beats.
note_durations_at_bpm.use: At a known BPM, compute the eighth-note duration and use it as the minimum plausible sung-note length.

beat_and_grid.rule: Most melody note onsets land ON a beat or a simple subdivision (eighth/sixteenth). A note starting far from the grid is likely a transcription glitch.
beat_and_grid.action: When in doubt about a stray onset, snap it to the nearest beat or eighth-note subdivision — but DO preserve genuine micro-timing/rubato (see Rhythm skill).

taal.definition: Hindustani rhythmic cycles: Teen Taal (16 beats), Keherwa (8), Dadra (6), Ek Taal (12), Jhaptaal (10).
taal.note: Given the tempo, the length of a phrase cycle in beats can suggest the taal.
